part: MPXV4006DP application note AN1646
notes: GENUINE Freescale application note AN1646, 'Noise Considerations for Integrated Pressure Sensors', Rev 2, 05/2005, 7 pp, FrameMaker 7.0, by Ador Reodique and Warren Schultz. Referenced by name from MPXV4006DP.pdf p.5 ('For additional output filtering, please refer to Application Note AN1646'). OUTPUT FILTERING, p.2 verbatim: 'a low-pass RC filter with a cutoff frequency of 650 Hz is recommended. A 750 ohm resistor and a 0.33 uF capacitor have been determined to give the best results (see Figure 2) since the 750 ohm series impedance is low enough for most A/D converters.' Figure 2 topology: sensor Vout -> 750 ohm series -> A/D node, 0.33 uF from that node to ground, supply decoupled 1.0 uF || 0.01 uF. calc: 1/(2*pi*750*0.33u) = 643 Hz, agrees with the stated 650. Figure 3 adds an MC33502 rail-to-rail buffer for A/Ds that cannot take the source impedance. Software: 8 to 64 sample rolling average; 10 samples -> ~2.5 mV pk-pk, 64 samples -> ~1 mV pk-pk, S/N improves as sqrt(N); four samples PLUS the RC filter also gives ~1 mV pk-pk. p.5 POWER SUPPLY: 5.0 V +/-5% supplying the sensor's maximum 10 mA; powering at any other voltage invalidates the offset, TCO and TCS trim; 0.33-1.0 uF || 0.01 uF ceramic decoupling; prefer a linear regulator such as MC78L05 over a switcher; tie the sensor supply and the A/D reference to the SAME supply so the output's ratiometricity cancels supply variation. p.5-6 LAYOUT: five rules (minimise loop areas; field-cancel by running equal opposite currents together; no 90-degree angles including T connections; single-point analog-to-power ground tie, made as close as possible to the A/D's VREFL; use ground planes selectively on analog boards), plus 'not advisable to have more than 1 inch between a de-coupling capacitor and the active device' with 50 mil traces. WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER: MOUNTING. There is NO mounting section and NO mounting-stress caution anywhere in the seven pages - that caution lives in Note 5 of MPXV4006DP.pdf p.3 ('external mechanical stresses and mounting position can affect the zero pressure output reading ... the device output must be autozeroed after installation ... assumes a maximum temperature change of +/-5 C between autozero and measurement'). NOTE ALSO that the datasheet's own Figure 3 output filter is a bare 470 pF with no series resistor, and the datasheet's accuracy curves are stated to be taken with THAT circuit, not with AN1646's 750 ohm / 0.33 uF - the two vendor recommendations are different circuits.

part: OPA2197IDR
notes: GENUINE TI datasheet SBOS737C, 'OPAx197 36-V, Precision, Rail-to-Rail Input/Output, Low Offset Voltage, Operational Amplifiers', JANUARY 2016 - REVISED MARCH 2018, 56 pages, covers OPA197/OPA2197/OPA4197. Rev C is the current rev served by ti.com on 2026-09-21. UNBLOCKS the previous BLOCKED row: ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa2197.pdf returned HTTP 200 application/pdf 2174683 B this session; the earlier HTTP 000 was an egress-proxy failure, not a dead URL. SETTLES THE TWO OPEN QUESTIONS IN hardware/controller/carrier.md. (1) Open-loop output impedance IS A SPECIFIED NUMBER, not only a curve: p.8 and p.10 both give 'ZO Open-Loop output impedance, f = 1 MHz, IO = 0 A, See Figure 26 ... 375 ohm' typ. THE REPO'S BACK-SOLVED Ro = 75.8 ohm IS REFUTED - it is 4.95x too small. Figure 26 (p.16, VS=+/-18V, RL=10k, CL=100pF, TA=25C) digitised: ~3.26 kohm at 0.1 Hz, 2.30 kohm at 1 Hz, 482 ohm at 10 Hz, a 371-379 ohm PLATEAU from 100 Hz to ~300 kHz (validating the digitisation against TI's own 375 ohm), then falling to ~301 ohm at 1 MHz, 221 at 2 MHz, 114 at 5 MHz and ~73 ohm at 10 MHz. The repo's 75.8 ohm happens to match the 10 MHz reading (= unity-gain crossover, GBW 10 MHz) but is NOT the specified figure. With ZO = 375 ohm the repo's reference-buffer poles move from 21 kHz to 4.24 kHz (100 nF) and from 200 Hz to 42 Hz (10.1 uF) - the instability is ~5x WORSE, so the case for R-ISO-REF is strengthened while every value derived from 75.8 ohm must be recomputed. (2) THE '1 nF MAXIMUM CAPACITIVE LOAD' IS A GENUINE OPA2197 FIGURE, so the disputing note at carrier.md:248-256 - which traced it to the INA828's feature list - is itself wrong. It appears three times: p.1 Features 'High Capacitive Load Drive Capability: 1 nF'; p.1 Description 'high capacitive load drive of up to 1 nF'; and section 7.3.5 'Capacitive Load and Stability' p.22 'in a unity-gain configuration, directly drives up to 1 nF of pure capacitive load'. The INA828 carries the same 1 nF headline (checked against the banked INA828IDR.pdf p.1) - the numbers merely coincide. NOTE the section is 7.3.5, not a 9.x. Small-Signal Overshoot vs Capacitive Load: Figures 27/28 (p.16) = Figures 47/48 (p.23), 100-mV output step, traces for RISO = 0/25/50 ohm, 20-2000 pF. Figure 48 is G = +1 V/V (unity gain, the configuration both Woody buffers use); digitised at RISO=0: 15.5% at 100 pF, 20.7% at 200 pF, 26.2% at 300 pF, ~30% at ~400 pF, 32.4% at 500 pF, 40.3% at 1 nF, ~45% at ~1.6 nF, 48.2% at 1950 pF. Figure 47 (G = -1 V/V) at RISO=0: 13.4% at 200 pF, 23.6% at 500 pF, 33.3% at 1 nF, ~42.5% at 2 nF. So '1 nF' is a stable-but-ringing limit (~40% overshoot bare), NOT a 30% threshold. ISOLATION RESISTOR IS RECOMMENDED: p.23 'inserting a small (10-ohm to 20-ohm) resistor, RISO, in series with the output', and Table 3 p.23 tabulates RISO for 45 deg / 60 deg phase margin: 100 pF -> 47.0/360.0 ohm; 1000 pF -> 24.0/100.0; 0.01 uF -> 20.0/51.0; 0.1 uF -> 6.2/15.8; 1 uF -> 2.0/4.7, with measured overshoot ~23%/~8.6% throughout. Cross-references TI Precision Design TIDU032. MOST USEFUL PAGE FOR WOODY: section 8.2.3 'Precision Reference Buffer' p.30 Figure 56 is a worked OPA197 reference buffer driving 10 uF with RISO = 37.4 ohm plus a dual feedback path (RF 1 Mohm at VOUT, RFx 10 kohm + CF 39 nF at the op-amp output), giving 89 deg phase margin and 4 kHz closed-loop BW, and states 'Any other load capacitances require recalculation of the stability components'. The repo's R-ISO-REF = 10 ohm is well under TI's 37.4 ohm for the same load. OTHER SPECS CONFIRMED: GBW 10 MHz typ; SR 20 V/us (VS=+/-18V, G=1, 10-V step) and 14 V/us at low supply; ISC +/-65 mA typ with continuous short to ground permitted (one amplifier per package); output swing from either rail 5 mV typ/25 mV max no-load, 95 mV typ/125 mV max at RL=10k, 430 mV typ/500 mV max at RL=2k; supply +/-2.25 to +/-18 V (4.5 to 36 V single), abs max 40 V; PSRR +/-1 uV/V typ, +/-3 uV/V max over -40..125 C (= 120 dB typ / 110.5 dB worst case - the repo's unsourced '114 dB' appears NOWHERE); IQ 1 mA typ / 1.3 mA max per amplifier, 1.5 mA max over temperature; VOS +/-25 uV typ / +/-100 uV max; dVOS/dT +/-0.5 uV/C typ / +/-2.5 uV/C max; AOL 143 dB typ / 120 dB min at RL=10k; en 5.5 nV/rtHz at 1 kHz; 0.1-10 Hz noise 1.30 uVpp; IB +/-5 pA typ. THERMAL, OPA2197 (section 6.5 p.6, DUAL - do not use the single OPA197 table on the same page): SOIC-8 D RthJA 107.9 C/W, RthJC(top) 53.9, RthJB 48.9, psiJT 6.6, psiJB 48.3, RthJC(bot) N/A; VSSOP-8 DGK RthJA 158. part: REF5050AIDR
notes: GENUINE TI datasheet SBOS410O, 'REF50xx Low-Noise, Very Low Drift, Wide VIN Precision Voltage Reference', JUNE 2007 - REVISED OCTOBER 2025, 52 pages, running head 'REF50, REF50E'. Covers REF5020/5025/5030/5040/5045/5050/5010 in I, AI and EI grades. URL CHANGED - the manifest's old source is a REAL 404, not a proxy failure: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ref5050.pdf returns HTTP 404 with TI's 3298-byte error page, as do .../symlink/ref5045.pdf and /lit/gpn/ref5050. TI renamed the product folder from REF50XX to REF50/REF50E at rev N (see section 11 Revision History), which broke the symlink. The working URL is the document-number form https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/sbos410/sbos410.pdf (HTTP 200, application/pdf, 5082549 B). *** GRADE REFUTATION - THE BOM'S PART NUMBER AND ITS STATED SPEC DO NOT MATCH. *** Table 4-2 'Device Performance Comparison' p.3 (NEW IN REV O) and section 3 Description p.1 both say the A suffix is the WORSE grade: REF50xxEI = Enhanced = 2.5 ppm/C, +/-0.025%, 0.5 uVpp/V, VIN max 42 V, IQ max 480 uA; REF50xxI = HIGH grade = 3 ppm/C, +/-0.05%, 3 uVpp/V, 18 V, 1.2 mA; REF50xxAI = STANDARD grade = 8 ppm/C, +/-0.1%, 3 uVpp/V, 18 V, 1.2 mA. So REF5050AIDR - the part on bom.csv:26 - is +/-0.1% initial accuracy and 8 ppm/C max drift. The '+-0.05%, 3ppm/degC' claimed at bom.csv:26 and again at docs/decisions/0003-breath-sensing-path.md:472, and the 'reference specified to 0.05%' at bom.csv:27, all describe REF5050IDR (no A). Section 6.5 p.7 confirms: Initial Accuracy High Grade -0.05/+0.05 %, Standard Grade -0.1/+0.1 %; dVOUT/dT High grade 2.5 typ / 3 max, Standard grade 3 typ / 8 max ppm/C over -40 to 125 C. Even the repo's 3 ppm/C is only the AI grade's TYPICAL. This is a ~2.7x hit to a ratiometric breath scale factor and needs either a part-number change or a re-budget. *** OUTPUT AND INPUT CAPACITORS - answers the C-REF-OUT qty-2 question: TI CALLS FOR A CAP ON BOTH PINS, so 'one in, one out' is the datasheet-consistent reading, but two is still short of TI's recommended layout. *** Section 8.4.1 Basic Connections p.26 verbatim: 'TI recommends a supply bypass capacitor ranging from 1uF to 10uF. Confirm that a output capacitor (CL) is connected from VOUT to GND. For output stability, verify that the equivalent series resistance (ESR) value of CL less than or equal to 1.5 ohm. To minimize noise, the recommended ESR of CL is from 1 ohm and 1.5 ohm.' Figure 8-6 annotates CBYPASS 1uF to 10uF on VIN, and CL = 1uF to 50uF for REF50xxI/REF50xxAI (1uF to 100uF for REF50xxEI). Section 9.4.1.1 'REF50xxI, REF50xxAI Layout Guidelines' p.29-30 lists FOUR capacitors: supply bypass 1uF to 10uF as close as possible to the supply and ground pins; 'Place a 1uF noise filtering capacitor between the NR pin and ground'; 'Verify that the output decouples with a 1uF to 50uF capacitor. A resistor in series with the output capacitor is optional. For better noise performance, the recommended ESR on the output capacitor is from 1 ohm to 1.5 ohm'; and 'Add a high-frequency, 1uF capacitor in parallel between the output and ground to filter noise and help with switching loads as data converters'. Section 9.3 p.29 separately says the VIN bypass may be 1uF to 50uF for I/AI - TI's own document is internally inconsistent on that range; 10 uF satisfies every version. ESR WARNING, which the BOM's bare 10uF X7R 1206 does not meet: section 9.2.1.2 p.28-29 'Very low equivalent series resistance (ESR) creates gain-peaking, which degrades SNR of the total system. If the ESR of the capacitor is not enough, then an additional resistor must be added in series with the output capacitor.' TI's own Figure 9-1 draws an explicit ESR resistor in series with the reference output capacitor, and Table 9-1 measures 86.7 dB SNR (10uF out, 0uF on NR) against 92.8 dB (10uF+47uF out, 1uF on NR). Section 8.3.6 p.26: a 1 uF on TRIM/NR makes a 10-20 Hz low-pass that 'decreases the overall noise measured on the VOUT pin by half' at the cost of start-up time. NOTE section 9.4.1.2 gives the EI grade the OPPOSITE ESR advice ('low ESR (maximum 1 ohm)') - do not carry an EI number onto an AI part. A HARD CAPACITIVE-LOAD TABLE EXISTS ONLY FOR THE EI GRADE (section 6.6 p.9: CIN stable input capacitor min 0.1 uF; CL stable output capacitor 1 to 100 uF, -40 to 125 C). For I/AI the limits come only from the 8.4.1 / 9.4.1.1 prose. part: Sub-miniature SPST toggle, 6 mm metric bushing (SW-POWER) - NKK Series M
notes: NKK Series M, 'Bushing Mount Miniature Toggles', 28 pages, catalogue section A51-A78, fetched direct from nkkswitches.com which answers 200 (it was never tried in earlier waves). SUPERSEDES THE BLOCKED ROW 'Sub-miniature SPST toggle 6 mm metric bushing (e.g. MTS-101)'. THE DIMENSIONS BELOW WERE READ BY RENDERING pages 7 and 11 AT 150 dpi - the drawings are vector and pdftotext returns nothing for them, so they are recorded here to save the next reader the render. *** SPST EXISTS AND IT IS M2011 *** (p.5 circuit table: 'SP M2011 ON NONE OFF, SPST'; p.11 note: 'M2011 model does not have terminal 1', i.e. it is the M2012 SPDT with one throw omitted). *** THREE TRUE M6 METRIC BUSHINGS, ALL MARKED 'M6 P0.75' ON THE DRAWING (p.7): *** S4 = 6mm/.350in (8.9mm) threaded with keyway; D4 = 6mm/.350in (8.9mm) threaded with D flat; D8 = 6mm splashproof with D flat, but D8 combines only with S/S2/S3 toggles and has a 10.0mm flange. THERE IS NO PLAIN ROUND 6 mm OPTION - every one has a keyway or a D flat. *** PANEL HOLE IS 6.5 mm DIAMETER, NOT 6.0 (p.7, 'Standard Hardware' panel drawings): *** S4 with keyway = 6.5 dia with a 5.6mm flat and 0.6mm feature; S4 with locking ring = 6.5 dia plus a separate 2.2mm dia anti-rotation hole at 6.5mm centres; D4 with D flat = 6.5 dia with a 5.8mm flat. MAX PANEL THICKNESS WITH STANDARD HARDWARE 2.6mm for S1/S4/D1/D4 (4.9mm for the splashproof D3/D8) - the module panel is 2mm aluminium, so it fits with 0.6mm spare, which is a constraint nobody had checked. Hardware supplied with S1/S4: 2 hex nuts, 1 locking ring, 1 lockwasher. With D1/D4: 2 hex nuts, 1 lockwasher, no locking ring. SINGLE-POLE BODY (p.11): front view 7.9mm across, 9.4mm deep behind the bushing, bushing thread 8.9mm long, toggle 10.5mm long x 2.8mm dia with a 25 degree throw, solder-lug terminal field 13.0 x 2.0mm on 4.7mm pitch, terminals 1.1 x 2.0mm. *** CONTACT MATERIAL IS NOT OPTIONAL HERE (p.10): *** W = silver over silver, POWER level, 6A@125VAC; G = gold over brass/copper, LOGIC level, 0.4VA max @ 28V; A = gold over silver, dual rated. SW-POWER drives the LT1641 ON pin, whose input current is 1 uA max - that is far below any silver contact's wetting current, so the part MUST be G or A. NOTE THAT THE CATALOGUE'S OWN EXAMPLE PART NUMBER, M2012SS1W01, USES W. Terminals: 01 solder lug, 02 quick connect, 03 straight PC. Electrical capacity p.1 also gives the logic-level applicable range as 0.1mA-0.1A @ 20mV-28V.

part: ME6217C33M5G
notes: The 3V3 LDO on the Waveshare ESP32-S3-Matrix, fed from net VCC_5V (i.e. VBUS behind D1 B5819WS), so everything on the board's 3V3 rail sits behind it. ME6217 series datasheet V05, 13 pp; the exact ordering code ME6217C33M5G appears in the p.2 selection guide - THIS IS WHY THIS COPY WAS BANKED IN PREFERENCE TO the LCSC C427602 upload (wmsc.lcsc.com/.../1912111437_..._C427602.pdf, V02, 10 pp), which is the same series document at an older revision, does not print the M5G code, and CARRIES NO THERMAL-RESISTANCE TABLE AT ALL - its only power-dissipation row is 1000 mW for SOT-89-5, a different package, which would over-budget a SOT-23-5 part by 67 %. COVERS: features p.1 (max output current 800 mA at VIN >= VOUT+1.0 V, dropout 100 mV at IOUT=300 mA for VOUT=5.0 V, operating range 2-6.5 V, output 1.5-5.6 V in 0.1 V steps, +/-1 % accuracy, 100 uA operating / 0.1 uA shutdown, 65 dB PSRR at 1 kHz, thermal shutdown 160 C); part-number decode and selection guide p.2 (ME6217C33M5G = VOUT 3.3 V, with CE, SOT23-5); pin configuration p.3 (SOT23-5: 1 VIN, 2 VSS, 3 CE, 4 NC, 5 VOUT); absolute maximum ratings p.4 (VIN 6.5 V, IOUT 800 mA, TOPR -40 to +85 C, TJ max 150 C, and THERMAL RESISTANCE JUNCTION-TO-AIR theta-JA = 210 C/W with PD = 0.6 W FOR SOT23-5, against 100 C/W and 1.25 W for both SOT-89 variants); electrical characteristics for ME6217A33/C33 p.4 (IOUTMAX typ 800 mA per Note 4; load regulation 10 mV typ / 50 mV max over 1-300 mA; DROPOUT VDIF typ 100 mV max 180 mV AT IOUT=300 mA - the only dropout point given; ISS 100 uA typ 130 uA max; ISD 0.1 uA typ; VCEH min 1.5 V, VCEL max 0.3 V; PSRR 65 dB; short-circuit current 350 mA typ; Tsd 160 C); C39 and C50 tables pp.5-6; Note 4 p.6; theory of operation, application notes and capacitor guidance pp.7-10; SOT23-5 outline and tape/reel pp.11-13. DOES NOT COVER: dropout voltage at any current above 300 mA - THERE IS NO DROPOUT FIGURE AT 800 mA anywhere in the document, so any such claim is extrapolation. VERDICT ON THE REPO'S UNSOURCED 800 mA (recorded in MANIFEST.csv row 35 as 'ME6217C33M5G LDO (3.3V, 800mA max)' from a vendor function-block PNG): CONFIRMED as the printed number but REFUTED as a usable ceiling, because Note 4 p.6 states verbatim 'IOUTMAX: Due to restrictions on the package power dissipation, this value may not be satisfied. Attention should be paid to the power dissipation of the package when the output current is large. This specification is guaranteed by design.' - i.e. not production-tested and conditioned on VIN >= VOUT+1.0 V. KEY DERIVED CONSEQUENCE (calc, from PD 0.6 W and theta-JA 210 C/W on p.4): with VIN = VCC_5V at about 4.5 V and VOUT 3.3 V the drop is 1.2 V, giving about 500 mA at Ta=25 C and about 357 mA at Ta=60 C; at a full 5.0 V input the 1.7 V drop gives only about 353 mA and 252 mA respectively. The real 3V3 ceiling is therefore roughly 250-500 mA, not 800 mA.

notes: Littelfuse SP050xBA Lead-Free/Green, 'TVS Diode Arrays - Surface Mount TVS Avalanche Diode Array'. 8 pages, internal PDF title 'CH05 silicon protection', printed page numbers 220-227 - it is a databook chapter extract, NOT a standalone part datasheet, and CARRIES NO DOCUMENT NUMBER AND NO REVISION DATE anywhere in it. This is a FAMILY document covering SP0502BA/SP0503BA/SP0504BA/SP0505BA/SP0506BA across nine package variants. SUPERSEDES THE BLOCKED ROW: the previous BLOCKED entry recorded www.farnell.com as 'HTTP 000 connect_rejected at the egress proxy'. That is no longer true - www.farnell.com/datasheets/47249.pdf, the exact URL already listed in that row's source_url field, returned HTTP 200 and 330885 bytes of real PDF on the first attempt this session. Other routes this session: datasheet.lcsc.com returned HTTP 200 but with an HTML body under a .pdf filename (discarded); www.littelfuse.com/assetdocs/... and m.littelfuse.com/media?... both 403. Worth re-probing farnell URLs in other BLOCKED rows. REFUTES THE PACKAGE IN FOUR REPO LOCATIONS. Ordering Information p.1 states SP0504BAHTG is 4 channels in SOT23-5, and SP0505BAHTG is 5 channels in SOT23-6. The outline drawings confirm it: p.6 is headed 'SP0504BAHTG - SOT23-5' with Package SOT23-5 / Pins 5 / JEDEC MO-178, while p.7 is headed 'SP0505BAHTG - SOT23-6' with Pins 6. So bom.csv U-TVS-SPI 'SOT-23-6 (0.95mm pitch)', carrier.md:825 'SP0504BAHT, SOT-23-6', carrier.md:812 and bom.csv U-TVS-CHAIN '4-ch array, SOT-23-6' are ALL WRONG on pin count - the 4-channel part is SOT-23-5. The '(0.95mm pitch)' half IS correct (e = 0.95 BSC, e1 = 1.90 BSC, both packages), so the ADR 0013 fine-pitch-policy reasoning survives. Either correct the package to SOT-23-5, or switch to SP0505BAHTG which genuinely is SOT-23-6 and gives a 5th channel. SETTLES THE POWER RATING, WHICH HAD NEVER HAD A SOURCE (datasheets/README.md:60). Absolute Maximum Ratings p.2: Package Power Dissipation SC70 0.2 W; SOT23-3, SOT23-5, SOT23-6, SOT143 0.225 W; TSSOP, MSOP 0.5 W. Independently corroborated on p.7 where the SOT23-6 dimension table's last row reads 'PD@70C .225W'. THE PRIOR REVIEW'S '0.98 W into SOT-23-6' IS REFUTED - it is 0.225 W, optimistic by 4.4x, and the figure is the same 0.225 W for SOT23-5 and SOT23-6 so it does not change with the package correction. PEAK PULSE POWER IS NOT-IN-DOCUMENT. There is NO I_PP, no peak pulse power dissipation, no 8/20us or 10/1000us waveform rating, no surge-current curve, no pulse-derating curve, and NO THERMAL RESISTANCE (thetaJA/thetaJC) for any package. The only occurrence of the word 'pulse' in all 8 pages is the p.3 graph caption 'Pulse-mode measurements, pulse width = 0.7 mS nominal', which is a V-I measurement condition and not a rating. This part is specified purely as an ESD-suppression array, so the 0.98 W line should be DELETED rather than corrected - there is no peak-pulse number to replace it with. Also NOT-IN-DOCUMENT: a distinct V_BR breakdown spec. COVERS, Electrical Specifications p.2 at TA=+25C: reverse standoff voltage 5.5 V min at I=10uA; reverse standoff leakage 1 nA typ / 100 nA max at V=5.0V; signal clamp positive 5.6/6.8/8 V at I=10mA and negative -1.2/-0.8/-0.4 V at I=10mA; clamp during 8 kV HBM ESD +12 V / -8 V typ; ESD test level IEC 61000-4-2 contact 20 kV (Level 4) and air 30 kV (Level 4) per p.1 Features, MIL-STD-883 Method 3015.7 HBM 30 kV; capacitance 30 pF typ at 2.5V/1MHz; turn on/off time <1 ns; operating -40 to 85C, storage -65 to 150C; diode dynamic resistance 1.0 ohm forward / 1.4 ohm reverse. Note 1: ESD applied between channel pins and ground one pin at a time, other channels open. CONFIRMS the 4-channel 5 V array claim (CH = 4, 'Input Protection for Applications Up to 5VDC'). Pin/channel map, read from the p.1 Pinout vector diagram rendered at 200 dpi (it does not extract as text): PIN 2 IS THE COMMON/GROUND, and pins 1, 3, 4, 5 are the four protected channels, each a back-to-back avalanche+forward pair to the common rail. All four channels share ONE common pin - there is no per-channel ground, so a single array cannot straddle PWR_GND and DIG_GND, which supports keeping U-TVS-SPI and U-TVS-CHAIN as two separate packages. TWO FACTS THE BOM ROW'S PHRASE '4-channel 5V array' DOES NOT CONVEY: (1) the array is effectively UNI-DIRECTIONAL - the negative clamp of -0.4/-0.8/-1.2 V at -10 mA is a plain forward diode drop, not an avalanche knee (p.3 V-I curve confirms), so it protects a 0 to +5 V signal referenced to the common pin and must NOT be reused on a bipolar CV node; (2) 30 pF per channel is HIGH for a signal-line TVS (p.1 Applications lists USB1.1 - this is a low-speed part by design). For Woody's SPI2 at 2 MHz behind the 100 ohm R-SPI-SER the 30 pF is acceptable: it is about 23 percent of the line's total capacitance including ~100 pF of 2 m Cat5, giving roughly a 29 ns edge against a 250 ns half-period, but this is the first time TVS capacitance has entered the umbilical edge budget at all. Also covers p.3 typical V-I characteristics and diode capacitance vs reverse voltage curves (capacitance falls from ~55 pF at 0 V to ~25 pF at 5 V), p.3 mechanical specifications (matte tin over copper alloy, molded epoxy, UL94-V-0, JEDEC MO-203 Issue A), and pp.4-8 outline drawings plus recommended pad layouts for SC70-3, SC70-5, SC70-6, SOT23, SOT143, SOT23-5, SOT23-6, TSSOP-8 and MSOP-8. DOCUMENT DEFECT NOTED: the p.2 electrical table writes the contact-discharge standard as 'IEC-61000-2'; the Features page and Description both correctly write 'IEC 61000-4-2'. Cite it as IEC 61000-4-2.

part: 74HC165 (ON Semiconductor)
notes: onsemi MC74HC165A / MC74HCT165A '8-Bit Serial or Parallel-Input/Serial-Output Shift Register', publication MC74HC165A/D, Rev. 13, April 2025, 16 pp. THIS IS THE DOCUMENT THAT SETTLES THE 3.3 V THRESHOLD QUESTION, AND IT CONTRADICTS THE REPO. It is the only 74HC165 datasheet of the four banked that CHARACTERISES THE PART AT 3 V: DC ELECTRICAL CHARACTERISTICS p.4 has VCC columns 2.0 / 3.0 / 4.5 / 6.0 V, and the 3.0 V row reads VIH min = 2.1 V and VIL max = 0.9 V - EXACTLY 0.70 / 0.30 x VCC, the ratio config/figures.yaml currently asserts 'BREAKS' below 4.5 V. Values are absolute volts, test condition 'Vout = 0.1 V or VCC - 0.1 V, |Iout| <= 20 uA', guaranteed over -55 to 25C / <=85C / <=125C. 3 V is a fully characterised rail here, not a stray line: Recommended Operating Ranges p.3 carries tr,tf 0-600 ns at VCC = 3.0 V and the AC table p.4 carries 3.0 V rows throughout. CONSEQUENCE: 3.3 V is BRACKETED by two published 0.70/0.30 rows (3.0 V and 4.5 V), so interpolating needs no assumption - VIH(3.3) = 2.1 + 0.2 x (3.15-2.1) = 2.31 V and VIL(3.3) = 0.9 + 0.2 x (1.35-0.9) = 0.99 V, which restore key-release-time to 119.9 us and key-press-time to 5.92 us. Transferability rests on all four banked 74HC165 documents agreeing digit for digit at every shared rail (2.0 V 1.5/0.5; 4.5 V 3.15/1.35; 6.0 V 4.2/1.8), these being JEDEC HC family thresholds; bom.csv U-KEYS lists manufacturer 'multiple' so this part is itself a legitimate fit. Also covers, at the 3.0 V rail specifically: fmax 18 MHz, tPLH/tPHL clock to QH 52 ns max, SH/LD to QH 58 ns, input H to QH 52 ns, output transition 27 ns; plus Cin 10 pF max, ICC 4 uA max at 25C/6.0 V, CPD 40 pF typ, IIK/IOK +/-20 mA. part: ESP32-S3-Matrix schematic
notes: VENDOR SCHEMATIC, finally obtained (HTTP 200, application/pdf, 177828 bytes). Altium Designer, 1 sheet A4, created 2024-03-25. THIS RETIRES THE BLOCKED ROW. SETTLES THE 5V-vs-3V3 QUESTION: all 64 LEDs have pin 1 VDD on net VCC_5V and pin 3 VSS on GND - no regulator, load switch, P-FET or diode between VCC_5V and the array. VCC_5V is USB VBUS through ONE SCHOTTKY, D1 = B5819WS (anode pin 1 on VBUS, cathode pin 2 = VCC_5V), so the LED rail is VBUS minus one Vf, NOT 5.00 V; C1 2.2uF sits on the VBUS side of D1. THE LED PART IS WS2812B-0807, NOT WS2812C - 64 instances U1..U64, value string verified on every symbol; this REFUTES ADR 0007 line 176, ROADMAP line 184 and ADR 0014 line 358, and the 5 mA/channel and 960 mA figures that rest on the WS2812C-2020 datasheet. DATA LINE: IO14 -> Q1 DMG1012T-7 N-channel MOSFET level shifter (gate pin 1 to 3V3, source pin 2 = IO14 with R4 2.2K pull-up to 3V3, drain pin 3 = LED_DIN with R3 4.7K pull-up to VCC_5V); NO SERIES RESISTOR anywhere on the data line; LED_DIN enters U8 pin 4 and the chain runs U8->U7->U6...->DOUT. 3V3 RAIL: U49 = ME6217C33M5G, pin 1 VIN from VCC_5V, pin 3 EN tied to VIN, pin 4 BP not connected, pin 5 VOUT = 3V3; input C3 0.1uF + C4 10uF, output C2 10uF. The 800 mA rating the manifest carries for this LDO is NOT on the schematic and remains unsourced. DECOUPLING ON THE LED RAIL: NONE INSIDE THE ARRAY - C1..C18 bounding boxes were extracted and none falls within the array extent; total VCC_5V capacitance is 11.1uF (C5 1uF at Q1, C3 0.1uF + C4 10uF at the LDO input). Extension pads are TP1 = DOUT, TP2 = VCC_5V, TP3 = GND. Also carries: MCU U66 = ESP32-S3FH4R2, R7/R9 22R in series on USB_N/USB_P, Y1 40MHz, J2 chip antenna CA-C03, IMU U67 = QMI8658C, R1/R2 5.1K CC pulldowns, header P1 20 pins. Does NOT give: any current rating, any LED current spec, the B5819WS Vf, or a PCB layout.
